summary.name: WhatsApp
summary.one_liner: WhatsApp is a free messaging and calling app from Meta for chatting, group messaging, voice and video calls, and sharing media on phones, computers, tablets, and watches.
use_cases: Making group voice or video calls
Organizing related groups in a community
summary.what_it_does: WhatsApp, from Meta, provides one-to-one and group chat with text, HD photos and videos, voice messages, and short video notes. Groups can be joined through invite links or QR codes, with admins able to approve join requests and set permissions, pin messages, and create events with RSVPs. Voice and video calls support up to 32 people, with screen sharing, effects, and reactions. Personal messages and calls are stated to be end-to-end encrypted, and users can turn on disappearing messages.
notable: End-to-end encryption for personal messages and calls
Events with RSVPs and polls inside group chats
Calls for up to 32 people with screen sharing
caveats: In-app purchases offered for an ad-free version, priced per account count (e.g. $4.00 for one account)
Mac version requires macOS 12.1 or later; app is 411.2 MB
Page lists data collection categories including location, contacts, and purchases linked to the user
